checks: The derivatives at h=k=0 are -A log eta and A log((T+eta)/eta). In the exact primitive the upper endpoint changes by k and the lower endpoint by h+k; subtracting those linear terms gives the stated Bregman difference.

Direct expansion of B_F at the lower endpoint gives eta times J((h+k)/eta) for every allowed h+k. The upper endpoint remains at least T/2 for small eta and bounded scaled directions, giving the claimed O(A eta^2/T) bound from F''=1/y.
J(0)=J'(0)=0 and J''(0)=1 imply the positive semidefinite rank-one Hessian in h,k, with null line h+k=0. The sign is for the singular part of the frozen negative-log term.
